name: Virtue Restaurant
tagline: James Beard Award-winning Southern American kitchen anchoring Hyde Park's dining scene.
description: Chef Erick Williams' James Beard Award-winning restaurant in Hyde Park celebrating the culinary heritage of the American South. Virtue serves beautifully executed Southern dishes in an elegant setting that honors both the food and its deep cultural origins.

name: Norman's Bistro
tagline: American Creole cuisine with a Brazilian flair in Chicago's vibrant Kenwood neighborhood.
description: A Kenwood neighborhood gem offering American Creole cuisine with Brazilian influences, set in a beautifully restored historic space. Norman's Bistro has been a Hyde Park dining anchor since 2010, known for inventive flavors, warm hospitality, and outstanding cocktails.

name: Justice of the Pies
tagline: Beloved Black-owned bakery serving sweet and savory pies baked with love and social purpose.
description: Maya-Camille Broussard's celebrated bakery bringing sweet and savory pies baked with love and social purpose to Chicago's South Side. Each pie tells a story, and every purchase supports criminal justice reform and community programs across Chicago.

name: Daisy's Po' Boy and Tavern
tagline: Hyde Park tavern serving Chicago's best po'boys with craft cocktails and a warm neighborhood vibe.
description: A Hyde Park neighborhood bar and kitchen serving Chicago's most satisfying po'boy sandwiches alongside craft cocktails and a warm, reliably welcoming atmosphere. Daisy's is the kind of neighborhood tavern every block in the city deserves.

name: Soul & Smoke Chicago
tagline: Chicago's fastest-growing BBQ born during the pandemic from community love and shared purpose.
description: Born during the pandemic from a community's demand for quality BBQ, Soul & Smoke has grown into one of Chicago's most celebrated barbecue restaurants. Operating in Evanston and Avondale, they deliver smoked meats with Southern soul and authentic Chicago heart.

name: Mikkey's Retro Grill
tagline: Hyde Park burger joint and late-night community anchor open until 4am daily.
description: A Hyde Park institution open until 4am, Mikkey's serves classic American burgers, shakes, and late-night comfort food to Chicago's South Side community. Reliable, delicious, and always open when you need it most — a true neighborhood anchor.

name: Uncle Remus Saucy Chicken
tagline: Chicago's legendary saucy chicken spot feeding the West Side community for 50+ years.
description: A Chicago West Side institution for over 50 years, Uncle Remus serves their legendary saucy fried chicken and hot links to generations of loyal fans. Multiple locations anchor the community with affordable, satisfying, iconic Chicago flavor that has never gone out of style.

name: Hyde Park Hair Salon
tagline: Historic barbershop since 1927 — where President Obama got his legendary haircut.
description: Chicago's historic barbershop since 1927, Hyde Park Hair Salon is where President Barack Obama got his haircut. Nearly a century of precision cuts and community service has made it one of the most storied and beloved barbershops in American history.

name: Esthetic Haus
tagline: Black woman-owned luxury brow bar and beauty spa redefining Chicago's skincare standards.
description: A luxury Black woman-owned brow bar and beauty spa in Wicker Park redefining Chicago's skincare standards. Esthetic Haus specializes in artful brow design, facials, and waxing services in a chic, welcoming environment designed for all skin tones.

name: Innate Allure
tagline: West Loop Black-owned skincare studio specializing in customized facials and brow lifts.
description: A West Loop Black-owned skincare studio offering customized facials, brow lifts, and targeted skin treatments for all complexions. Known for exceptional personalized service and results-driven skincare protocols that keep clients glowing.

name: Burrell Communications Group
tagline: One of America's largest multicultural marketing agencies pioneering Black advertising since 1971.
description: Founded in 1971, Burrell Communications Group is one of America's largest and most influential multicultural marketing agencies, headquartered in Chicago. For over 50 years, Burrell has pioneered authentic African American marketing for Fortune 500 brands including McDonald's, Toyota, and Procter & Gamble.

name: myWHY Agency
tagline: All-women Black-owned agency serving purpose-driven brands with powerful strategic storytelling.
description: A Chicago-based all-women Black-owned agency at the intersection of strategy and storytelling, serving purpose-driven brands and nonprofits. myWHY is known for bold creative work that connects organizations to their audiences with authentic cultural resonance.

name: The Silver Room
tagline: Hyde Park's eclectic jewel for handmade jewelry, fashion, art, and music since 1997.
description: A Hyde Park treasure since 1997, The Silver Room is Chicago's eclectic destination for handmade jewelry, fashion, art, music, and community. Beyond retail, The Silver Room hosts the beloved annual Silver Room Block Party celebrating Black art, culture, and local commerce.

name: Black Ensemble Theater
tagline: Chicago theater company combating racism through transformative African American theatrical arts.
description: Founded in 1976 by Jackie Taylor, Black Ensemble Theater is Chicago's powerhouse Black theater company committed to eradicating racism through transformative African American theatrical productions. A cultural institution that has launched careers, changed minds, and enriched Chicago's arts community.

name: Da Book Joint
tagline: South Side Chicago's cherished Black bookstore championing African American fiction since 2007.
description: A South Side Chicago Black bookstore championing African American fiction, history, and culture since 2007. Da Book Joint is a community anchor where readers find books that speak directly to their lives, histories, and imaginations — often titles you won't find elsewhere.

name: Coffee Hip Hop & Mental Health
tagline: Black-owned mental health coffee space using hip hop culture to heal Chicago communities.
description: A West Side Chicago space using hip hop culture as a vehicle for healing, community-building, and mental health destigmatization. Coffee Hip Hop & Mental Health hosts workshops, open mics, and counseling sessions rooted in the belief that Black mental health matters and healing can happen in community.

name: Forty Acres Fresh Market
tagline: Black-owned grocery market fighting food insecurity on Chicago's underserved West Side.
description: A Black-owned grocery market fighting food insecurity on Chicago's West Side by providing fresh produce, healthy staples, and affordable groceries to underserved communities. Forty Acres represents the powerful intersection of entrepreneurship, community investment, and food justice.

name: MADD Rhythms
tagline: Family-owned Black tap dance company preserving Chicago's vibrant rhythmic arts tradition.
description: A family-owned Black tap dance company preserving Chicago's vibrant tap dance tradition through world-class performance, education, and community programming. MADD Rhythms celebrates African American rhythmic arts and trains the next generation of Chicago performers.
address_line_1: 4701 S King Dr Use 47th Street Entrance

name: Brown Sugar Bakery
tagline: South Side bakery known for cakes, cobblers, pies and sweets
description: A Greater Grand Crossing bakery offering cheesecakes, cupcakes, cobblers, cookies and pies. The brand has grown to include a Navy Pier shop and a candy operation.

name: Nafsi
tagline: Elevated soul food inside the historic South Shore Cultural Center
description: A Black-owned restaurant serving elevated takes on classics like shrimp and grits, fried green tomatoes, chicken and waffles, and beignets, located on Lake Michigan in South Shore.

name: Momentum Coffee
tagline: Black-owned cafe and coworking concept with multiple South and West Side locations
description: A Black- and family-owned coffee shop and coworking concept with locations including South Loop, North Lawndale, Englewood and Austin.

name: Chicago French Press
tagline: Black-owned and woman-owned coffee company in Chicago
description: A Black- and woman-owned coffee company producing single-origin organic arabica coffee and hand-blended loose-leaf tea, donating a share of sales to underserved communities.

name: Park Manor 75
tagline: Chatham's Black-owned wine and charcuterie bar
description: A Black-owned wine and charcuterie bar in Chatham serving curated wines, craft cocktails, mocktails and charcuterie boards, with a menu featuring wines and spirits from Black-owned businesses.

name: Brûlée Chicago
tagline: Refined Southern brunch in the South Loop from a Black women-owned team
description: A Black women-owned Southern brunch restaurant in the South Loop serving dishes like lobster and sweet potato waffles and an avocado croast.

name: Haji Healing Salon
tagline: Affordable social wellness on the South Side: yoga, acupuncture, reiki, and meditation
description: A Black-owned social wellness enterprise offering low-cost yoga, meditation, community-style acupuncture, reiki, bodywork, and herbalism, priced to remove barriers for Black and brown Chicagoans seeking healing.

name: Studio Yogi
tagline: A welcoming Black woman-owned hot yoga studio in South Shore
description: A Black woman-owned yoga studio offering hot vinyasa, yin, candlelight sound journeys, and community classes to bring accessible yoga and wellness to the South Shore community.

name: CBQ Facial Beauty Bar
tagline: Black-owned facial and skincare bar in Bronzeville
description: A Black-owned facial and skincare bar offering personalized hydro-facials, skin assessments, brow services, and skin-health workshops, staffed by a team of licensed estheticians.

name: Hanahana Beauty
tagline: Chicago-based clean skincare brand rooted in ethically sourced Ghanaian shea butter
description: A Black-owned clean skincare and wellness brand founded in Chicago, built on shea butter sourced directly from women producers in Tamale, Ghana, and known for ethical sourcing and African beauty traditions.

name: Woodlawn Dental Gallery
tagline: Black-owned general dentistry serving Woodlawn and Hyde Park
description: A Black-owned general dental practice providing general and personalized dental care to the Woodlawn, Hyde Park, and Chatham communities.

name: Robin L. Ferguson, DDS
tagline: African American woman-owned dental practice on Chicago's South Side
description: A Black woman-owned general and cosmetic dentistry practice on Chicago's South Side. Services include crowns, veneers, implants, root canals, and sleep apnea treatment.

name: Del-Kar Pharmacy
tagline: Independent Black-owned pharmacy serving North Lawndale
description: A Black-owned independent pharmacy in North Lawndale, reported as one of the oldest Black-owned drugstores in Chicago, helping keep the neighborhood from becoming a pharmacy desert.

name: Essential Elements Chicago
tagline: Black and woman-owned South Side boutique for clothing, shoes, and accessories
description: A Black and woman-owned boutique on Chicago's South Side curating clothing, shoes, and accessories, including pieces from European designers and independent makers.

name: Mahalia's Gift Shop
tagline: Chatham gift shop featuring dozens of Black-owned brands
description: A Black-owned, consignment-based gift shop in Chatham named after gospel legend Mahalia Jackson, carrying apparel, accessories, beauty products, and home goods from over 40 Black-owned brands.

name: Recycled Modern
tagline: Curated vintage home decor store, art gallery, and event lounge spotlighting Black creatives
description: A Hyde Park home decor store, art gallery, and event lounge featuring vintage and handcrafted goods with a focus on Black artists and designers.

name: Gallery Guichard
tagline: Bronzeville fine art gallery specializing in art of the African Diaspora
description: A Black-owned art gallery in Chicago's Bronzeville district exhibiting multicultural artists who specialize in the art of the African Diaspora.

name: Faie Afrikan Art
tagline: Bronzeville gallery showcasing African and African Diaspora fine art
description: A Black-owned art gallery in Bronzeville featuring African art from across the continent alongside works by local artists from the Diaspora.

name: Digifé
tagline: Black-owned video production company documenting impactful stories for brands and communities
description: A Chicago video production company producing documentaries, branded content, and digital series, built to put more Black and brown creatives behind the camera.

name: The.BlkRoom
tagline: Coworking and creator studio for Black creatives on the West Side
description: A Garfield Park coworking and maker space that gives Black creatives affordable access to studios, equipment, and programming.

name: Summerset Studios
tagline: Black-owned Chicago wedding and event photography and videography
description: A Black-owned Chicago photography and videography studio specializing in multicultural wedding photography and corporate event photography.

name: Call & Response Books
tagline: Hyde Park bookstore prioritizing books by authors of color
description: A Black woman-owned independent bookstore in Hyde Park that prioritizes selling books by and about Black people and other people of color, with author talks and community events.

name: Honey & Hue Bookstore
tagline: Beverly bookstore centering BIPOC stories and community
description: A Black-owned bookstore in the Beverly neighborhood specializing in books relating to Black, Indigenous, and people-of-color experiences while carrying books for everyone.

name: CZL P.C.
tagline: Black woman-owned law firm offering corporate legal counseling and DEI consulting
description: A Chicago-based Black woman-owned law firm and registered Benefit Corporation providing corporate legal counseling and DEI consulting to entrepreneurs, minority-owned businesses, nonprofits, and government agencies.

name: Jimerson Tax and Accounting Chicago
tagline: Black-owned and women-owned accounting and tax advisory firm in Chicago
description: A Chicago accounting and tax advisory firm partnering with business owners on tax strategy, bookkeeping, and financial planning, describing itself as a Black-owned, women-owned firm.

name: 4Degrees
tagline: Chicago Black-founded AI relationship-intelligence CRM platform
description: A Chicago-based software company building an AI-powered relationship intelligence CRM for relationship-driven industries such as venture capital, banking, and commercial real estate.

name: Zora Digital
tagline: Certified women- and minority-owned digital marketing agency in Chicago
description: A Chicago digital strategy and marketing agency offering website design and development, paid media, analytics, and digital strategy for purpose-led brands and nonprofits.

name: Glasshouse Interior
tagline: Black-owned interior design firm and home decor showroom on the South Side
description: An interior design firm and home decor store offering residential and commercial design plus private-label drapery, artwork, and furniture from its Armour Square showroom.

name: Black Luxe Candle Co.
tagline: Black-owned candle shop and candle-making classroom in Wicker Park
description: A candle shop selling handmade candles and wax products and running candle-making classes from its Wicker Park retail store.

name: UJAMAA Construction, Inc.
tagline: Chicago diversity general contractor and construction manager
description: A Chicago general contracting, construction management, and design-build firm. It is a Black/minority-owned diversity contractor serving the Midwest and Southeast.

name: AFRORACK
tagline: Music and audio-arts education serving Black and brown youth
description: A Chicago music education institution that provides children and young adults of color access to modular synthesizers and sound design tools through STEM-focused programming.

name: ELMS Events & Production
tagline: Black woman-owned event planning and production agency
description: A Chicago event planning and production agency focused on galas, weddings, brand activations, and community programming.

name: Ani Real Estate
tagline: Chicago Black-owned full-service real estate brokerage
description: A Chicago Black-owned real estate brokerage and team serving buyers and sellers across the Chicago metro, with a focus on agent mentorship and opportunity.
address_line_1: 7300 S Cottage Grove Ave Suite B

name: Gorée Cuisine
tagline: West African and Afro-Caribbean flavors in a warm, welcoming Bronzeville setting.
description: West African and Afro-Caribbean restaurant in Bronzeville serving vibrant Senegalese and Caribbean dishes including thiéboudienne, griot, and mafé in a beautifully warm and welcoming dining room.

name: Liberty Bank and Trust
tagline: Black-owned New Orleans bank with a full-service branch in Forest Park
description: Liberty Bank and Trust, a Black-owned bank founded in New Orleans in 1972, runs a full-service branch on Roosevelt Road in Forest Park, just west of Chicago. The branch offers personal and business banking and lending.

_verified.note: On the FDIC MDI list (Q2 2026) as Black-owned, and its site lists the Forest Park branch in October 2026. Forest Park is a suburb about 10 miles west of the Loop. FDIC lists this as the Roosevelt Road branch, opened 2015. A Chicago loan office at 850 W Jackson Blvd is marked Coming Soon on the bank's site. Weekend hours not published. FDIC MDI code 1 (Black-owned).

name: GN Bank
tagline: Black-owned community bank on King Drive in Bronzeville
description: GN Bank is a Black-owned savings bank with one office on South King Drive in Chicago's Bronzeville neighborhood. It traces its history to 1934 and took the GN Bank name in 2018, after operating as Illinois Service Federal. It offers personal deposit accounts and lending.

_verified.note: On the FDIC MDI list (Q2 2026) as Black-owned, and its site posts 2026 holiday notices. Use gnbank.net. The gnbank.com domain is parked and for sale. The Chatham branch is no longer listed and FDIC shows one office. Hours left blank because the site's text is unclear: it reads Monday to Friday 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM, Wednesday 8:30 AM to 12:00 PM, Saturday 8:30 AM to 12:00 PM, Sunday closed. Call to confirm before publishing hours. A CBS Chicago segment headlined complaints against the bank's practices; this pass did not review it, so look before featuring. FDIC MDI code 1 (Black-owned).

name: First Independence Bank
tagline: Black-owned Detroit bank with a Chicago branch on East Ontario Street
description: First Independence Bank is a Black-owned bank founded in Detroit in 1970, headquartered in Detroit, with a branch in Chicago. It took over the deposits and River North office of Metropolitan Capital Bank and Trust when that bank failed in January 2026. It offers personal and business banking and lending.

_verified.note: On the FDIC MDI list (Q2 2026) as Black-owned, and it opened its Chicago branch on 2026-01-30 by acquiring Metropolitan Capital Bank and Trust. The Chicago branch is the former Metropolitan Capital Bank and Trust office, acquired 2026-01-30 after that bank failed. Headquarters 7310 Woodward Ave, Detroit. The site blocks simple fetches, so it was read with a browser user agent. FDIC MDI code 1 (Black-owned).

name: For Members Only Federal Credit Union
tagline: Digital credit union for members of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority
description: For Members Only Federal Credit Union is a digital credit union sponsored by Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated and owned by its members. It calls itself the first Black-owned, woman-led, sorority-based digital financial institution in the United States. Banking is done online.

_verified.note: On the NCUA MDI list (June 30, 2026) under Black Americans and active per NCUA, and its site is current for 2026. Who can join: members of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority (single common bond). It is not open to the general public, so list it only if member-only institutions fit the directory. It is digital-only. The contact address, 5656 S Stony Island Ave, is the sorority's headquarters and not a branch, so the street address is left blank. Hours are Central time contact hours. Phone is from the NCUA record. Founded year is the NCUA charter year.

name: South Side Community Federal Credit Union
tagline: Community development credit union for Chicago's South Side
description: South Side Community Federal Credit Union is a low-income designated community development credit union and certified CDFI on South Wentworth Avenue in Chicago. It opened in November 2003 and also runs a HUD-approved housing counseling program. It offers savings, share draft checking, loans and small business accounts.

_verified.note: On the NCUA MDI list (June 30, 2026) under Black Americans and active per NCUA, with published hours and address. Who can join: people and businesses that live, work, worship, attend school or belong to an organization on Chicago's South Side, from 22nd Street south to the city limits and from the lake west to Western Avenue. Tuesday is drive-thru only. The site lists the address as 5401 South Wentworth Avenue #25 Suite 19E. Its footer still says 2023, so activity rests on NCUA reporting as of June 30, 2026.

name: Urban Growers Collective
tagline: Black- and women-led nonprofit farm with a CSA and mobile market on the South Side
description: Urban Growers Collective runs 8 farms on 11 acres across Chicago and sells produce through a CSA, the Fresh Moves mobile market, farm stands and farmers markets. It was founded in 2017 by Erika Allen and Laurell Sims, and Allen has led it as CEO since 2024.

_verified.note: Own site calls it a Black- and women-led nonprofit farm, and the 2026 CSA and fall 2026 events are live. Nonprofit. Address is the public South Chicago Farm; the office is at 1200 W 35th St #118, Chicago 60609. Upcoming events on site: Harvest Fest 10/10 and a Winter Grower Workshop 11/7. Stand hours vary by season so hours left empty.

name: Eden Place Farms
tagline: Fuller Park farm and farm store growing greens, herbs and microgreens
description: Eden Place Farms grows greens, herbs, collards and microgreens on about 3 acres in Fuller Park and is part of the IL-EATS food hub. It runs under Fuller Park Community Development, co-founded by Michael and Amelia Howard, with a mission to reconnect the African American community to farming. A farm store opened in June 2025.

_verified.note: Buy Fresh Buy Local profiles it as Black-owned, and Illinois Extension reported its farm store opening in June 2025. Nonprofit. Farm is near W 43rd Pl and S Shields Ave, but no exact street address is published, so address left empty. No phone or store hours found. Instagram has posts from late 2025.

name: We Sow We Grow
tagline: West Pullman community farm teaching neighbors to grow food
description: We Sow We Grow is an education nonprofit that grows fruits and vegetables on a West Pullman lot and shares eggs with neighbors. Natasha Nicholes founded it in 2016. It also sells merchandise to support its programs.

_verified.note: ABC7 Chicago covered Natasha Nicholes and the West Pullman farm in February 2026. Nonprofit, education focus rather than a retail farm. ZIP not published. No phone found.

name: Sistas In The Village
tagline: Black woman-led Englewood farm selling and sharing produce at local markets
description: Sistas In The Village grows produce on a lot in Englewood and sells and donates it at markets including the Englewood Village Market. Co-founders Mecca Bey and Nyabweza Itaagi started it in 2020. They also run growing workshops.

_verified.note: Block Club Chicago describes it as a Black woman-led farm, and the Driehaus Foundation featured it in February 2026. Address is the public farm lot. Phone comes from the RAG Englewood business directory listing. Sells mostly at markets, so no hours.

name: Sowed Up Farms
tagline: Black women-owned West Side farm with produce boxes and market stands
description: Sowed Up Farms is a family-operated urban farm on Chicago's West Side that sells produce boxes and sells at neighborhood farmers markets. It is led by founder Chamika. October 2026 dates include the Eckhart Park and Austin Town Hall markets.

_verified.note: Own site says Black women-owned and family-operated, and it lists October 2026 market dates. Markets only for in-person sales: Eckhart Park Farmers Market Oct 3, 10, 17 at 9am and Austin Town Hall Farmers Market Oct 25 at 1pm. Farm address not published.

name: Westside Bee Boyz
tagline: North Lawndale beekeepers selling honey, honey drinks and body care
description: Westside Bee Boyz keeps hives around Chicago, including at O'Hare, and sells honey, honey water, honey soda, soaps and lotions. Thad Smith founded it in 2014 in North Lawndale. It also offers hive services and sells at farm stands that take LINK/EBT.

_verified.note: Austin Weekly News profiles founder Thad Smith as an African American beekeeper, and Instagram shows posts June to October 2026. Old website westsidebeeboyz.com is now spam, never link it. Website left empty; use the Linktree. Honey business rather than a crop farm.

name: Black Oaks Center
tagline: Black-led farm and food hub in Pembroke Township selling Black farmers' produce
description: Black Oaks Center for Sustainable Renewable Living runs a farm and education center in Pembroke Township, Illinois. Its Healthy Food Hub sells produce from Black farmers. It was founded by Dr. Jifunza Wright-Carter, Fred Carter and Akin Carter and has been active since 2011.

_verified.note: NCAT's internship listing, updated April 2026, calls it a Black-led nonprofit and shows current programs. Nonprofit. About 65 miles south of Chicago. Active since 2011; exact founding year not confirmed, so left empty. No public hours.

name: Faith Farms & Orchard
tagline: Gary urban farm and orchard growing food for wholesale and the local food bank
description: Faith Farms & Orchard is run by Families Anchored In Total Harmony CDC, founded in 2013 by Rev. Curtis Whittaker to revive his Gary neighborhood. It grows produce, keeps chickens, goats and bees, and runs the Faith Fresh Frozen program. About 80% of its harvest goes wholesale and about 20% is donated to the Food Bank of Northwest Indiana.

_verified.note: Capital B Gary covered the farm in 2024, and it won the 2025 Marbleseed Changemakers award and runs the Faith Fresh Frozen program. In Gary, Indiana, listed under Chicago. Nonprofit. Capital B (a Black news outlet) quotes Whittaker saying everyone on the project was Black and brown; no source states his race in words. 2025 activity is the Marbleseed Changemakers award. Website faithgary.org had an SSL error, so website left empty. Address is the farm site named in coverage; confirm it is open to visitors before listing as a visit location.
